title: RAG Evaluation & Anti-Hallucination: Recall@K, MRR & Faithfulness Checks
summary: Stop tuning RAG by vibes: build CI-friendly Retrieval metrics (Recall@K, MRR) and Groundedness / Faithfulness verifiers that catch numeric hallucinations before deployment.
aeo_capsule: Production RAG Evaluation separates retrieval quality from generation fidelity: Recall@K measures how much ground-truth evidence enters the Top-K pool, MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank) rewards placing the first relevant document at rank 1, and deterministic groundedness checks (check_numeric_faithfulness()) catch unverified numeric hallucinations before answers reach users. This chapter implements a CI-ready verification suite in zero-dependency Python 3.12 (examples/ai_ch04_rag_eval.py).
learning_objectives: Decouple retrieval evaluation (Recall@K, MRR) from generation faithfulness so you diagnose missing context versus LLM fabrication accurately.
Implement a deterministic numeric groundedness verifier that flags unverified rates, amounts, and version numbers before deployment.
Wire a version-controlled Golden Eval Set into GitHub Actions CI/CD to prevent silent regressions whenever chunking, indexes, or prompts change.

sections.heading: 4.1 Quantifying Retrieval Quality: Recall@K and MRR in Practice
paragraphs: Many engineering teams iterate on RAG by spot-checking five prompts and shipping whenever the answers 'look better' (vibe-based evaluation). Weeks later, a seemingly harmless tweak to chunk size silently cuts recall in half on critical queries. Turning RAG from a black box into a debuggable system begins by evaluating Retrieval and Generation independently. At the retrieval layer, two lightweight metrics carry most of the diagnostic signal: Recall@K measures what fraction of relevant ground-truth documents appear inside the Top-K results—critical in medical, legal, and compliance domains where missing a single clause is unacceptable—while Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) measures how close to rank 1 the first relevant document lands, directly defending against the 'Lost in the Middle' attention decay in long prompts.

Every reliable evaluation pipeline starts with a version-controlled Golden Eval Set stored in JSONL inside Git, containing each query, its verified relevant document IDs, and reference facts. In recall_at_k(), we guard against empty relevant sets or non-positive K, then compute the intersection ratio between set(retrieved_ids[:k]) and relevant_ids. In mean_reciprocal_rank(), we scan each ranked list and stop at the very first relevant hit to record 1 / rank. Be careful with one subtle mathematical distinction: only truncated MRR@1 equals Recall@1 and Hit@1 when each query has exactly one relevant document. When multiple documents are relevant, Recall@1 is capped at 1 / len(relevant_ids), while full-list MRR still counts hits beyond rank 1 with decaying reciprocal weight.

Walking through this chapter's verified output—'Ch.04 Recall@2: 0.667 | MRR: 0.611'—shows why tracking both numbers pays off immediately. Across the three runs in eval_runs: query 1 places doc_1 at rank 2 (Recall@2 = 1.0, RR = 1/2 = 0.500); query 2 places doc_3 at rank 1 (Recall@2 = 1.0, RR = 1/1 = 1.000); query 3 places doc_7 at rank 3 (Recall@2 = 0.0, RR = 1/3 ~ 0.333). Averaging yields Recall@2 = (1 + 1 + 0) / 3 = 0.667 and MRR = (0.5 + 1.0 + 0.3333) / 3 = 11 / 18 ~ 0.611. If your production pipeline passes only Top-2 chunks to the LLM, query 3 never sees doc_7—meaning no amount of prompt engineering can fix it until you improve retrieval.
bullets: Recall@K tracks Top-K coverage of ground-truth documents, protecting multi-evidence and high-compliance workflows from missed hits.
MRR averages 1 / rank of the first relevant document, directly exposing whether your ranker puts the best evidence at the top.
On the live 3-query fixture, Recall@2 = 0.667 exposes a 1/3 Top-2 truncation miss while MRR = 0.611 quantifies top-rank loss.
sections.callout_title: Engineering Note: The Recall@K vs. MRR Diagnostic Matrix
sections.callout_body: High Recall@10 (e.g., 0.95) paired with low MRR (e.g., 0.35) means your retriever finds the right documents but ranks them too low—tune RRF or add a Cross-Encoder reranker. Low Recall@10 means relevant chunks never entered the candidate pool at all—fix chunking, tokenization, or embeddings before touching rerankers.

sections.heading: 4.2 Generative Faithfulness: Deterministic Numeric & Entity Groundedness Checks
paragraphs: Even when retrieval achieves stellar Recall@K and MRR, LLMs can still ignore retrieved context or blend in stale pretraining memory to fabricate numbers. In our example, the retrieved tax snippet states a 10% treaty rate and a 30% default Non-Resident Alien (NRA) withholding rate—yet an unguarded model can still hallucinate 'The rate is 15% under default rules.' Numeric hallucinations are catastrophic in finance, pricing, healthcare, and legal assistants, yet they are also the easiest hallucinations to intercept at microsecond speed. Our check_numeric_faithfulness() function uses zero-cost regular expressions to extract every numeric token from both retrieved chunks and the model answer, flagging any orphan numbers absent from the source corpus.

The regex \b\d+(?:\.\d+)?%? captures integers, decimals, and percentages (such as 30%, 10%, and 15%) in microseconds. On the grounded response ('Default NRA rate is 30%, treaty rate is 10%.'), the checker returns True with an empty missing list; on the fabricated response ('15%'), it returns False and pinpoints ['15%']. Before deploying this rule in production, handle two common formatting traps: strip thousands separators and currency symbols (otherwise '1,000' splits into '1' and '000'), and normalize written numbers or decimals (such as 'ten percent' or '0.10' versus '10%') prior to set comparison to eliminate false positives.

When the groundedness checker catches an unverified number, avoid throwing a raw 500 error. Build an 'intercept -> retry -> safe fallback' loop: feed the unverified token list (['15%']) back into a constrained retry prompt instructing the model to cite only explicitly sourced figures with chunk IDs; if the second attempt still fails verification, gracefully return a safe refusal with links to the retrieved source passages. For non-numeric factual claims (people, conditions, causal statements), layer a lightweight LLM-as-a-Judge verifier behind the fast deterministic numeric gate.
bullets: Deterministic numeric groundedness catches fabricated rates and amounts in microseconds with zero extra LLM API cost.
Normalize thousands separators (1,000), currency symbols, and written percentages ('ten percent' -> 10%) before set comparison.
Pair hard numeric interception with a constrained retry and safe fallback, adding LLM-as-a-Judge for non-numeric semantic claims.
sections.callout_title: Pitfall Guide: Valid Arithmetic Derivation vs. Hallucination
sections.callout_body: If the source says 'list price $100 with a $20 discount' and the model answers '$80', naive string matching will flag '80' as ungrounded. In calculation-heavy domains, require the LLM to call a deterministic calculator tool (see Ch.05 Tool Calling) and append the tool output to the trusted source set.

sections.heading: 4.3 CI/CD Integration: Enforcing Golden Eval Thresholds in GitHub Actions
paragraphs: An evaluation script that lives only inside a developer's local notebook goes stale within two weeks. Production teams wrap recall_at_k(), mean_reciprocal_rank(), and check_numeric_faithfulness() into standard Python unittest or pytest suites executed automatically by GitHub Actions on every Pull Request. Whenever a commit alters chunk boundaries, BM25 parameters, stop words, or prompt templates, CI replays the Golden Eval Set: if Recall@5 drops below 0.85, MRR drops below 0.75, or any compliance fixture emits an ungrounded number, the build fails and blocks the merge—eliminating silent regressions.

The main reason teams abandon CI evals is slow feedback and flaky API costs: running 2,000 full cloud LLM calls on every commit takes 15+ minutes and fails randomly on rate limits. The proven solution is a tiered evaluation pyramid. On every Pull Request (Fast Gate, under 3 minutes), run strictly deterministic offline retrieval metrics (caching model weights in ~/.cache or using precomputed vectors) plus deterministic numeric groundedness tests. Reserve full multi-thousand-item end-to-end generation and LLM-as-a-Judge scoring for scheduled Nightly runs that publish trend dashboards.

To keep CI trustworthy, enforce strict reproducibility: pin exact embedding model versions and checksums, set temperature = 0 with fixed seeds for evaluation runs, and archive structured JSON metric artifacts (e.g., Recall@2=0.667, MRR=0.611, Faithfulness=100%) on every build. When a PR causes a regression, diffing the per-query output immediately reveals which specific queries dropped from hit to miss, turning code reviews from subjective debates into objective evidence.
bullets: Package Recall@K, MRR, and numeric faithfulness checks as standard unittest gates that block regressive PR merges.
Use a tiered eval pyramid: fast deterministic retrieval + numeric checks on every PR (<3 min), full LLM-as-a-Judge runs nightly.
Pin embedding model versions, enforce temperature = 0, and cache model weights in CI to eliminate flaky builds.
sections.callout_title: Best Practice: Never Gate PRs on High-Variance LLM Judges
sections.callout_body: Keep PR merge blockers 100% deterministic and reproducible (Recall@K, MRR, JSON schema validation, numeric groundedness). Track probabilistic semantic judge scores in Nightly regression charts and alert on statistically significant drift.

sections.heading: 4.4 The Hallucination Interception Net: Tiered Production Guardrails
paragraphs: An offline Golden Eval Set catches known failure modes, but real production users inevitably submit typos, edge-case negations, and out-of-domain questions. Complete anti-hallucination engineering therefore connects CI evals with live production observability. By logging retrieval candidates and generation outputs separately in structured telemetry, your dashboard tracks three vital signs continuously: empty-retrieval rate (coverage), top-rank click or citation position (ranking quality), and numeric faithfulness retry rate (groundedness). Any drift immediately reveals whether the root cause is stale documents, degraded ranking, or prompt regression.

Avoid one-size-fits-all guardrails across every product surface; calibrate enforcement to business risk. Internal knowledge search or casual support bots can treat numeric mismatches as soft warnings accompanied by inline source links to preserve speed and fluidity. High-stakes financial tax calculators (like our dividend withholding example), clinical assistants, and contract-review tools must enforce Fail-Closed guardrails: refuse to answer when retrieval similarity falls below cutoff, and trigger a constrained retry or human handoff on any unverified figure—because saying 'I cannot verify this number' is infinitely safer than stating a wrong rate.

Finally, close the loop into an Eval Flywheel: periodically anonymize and sample live failure cases (empty retrievals, blocked numeric hallucinations, and user thumbs-down queries) back into your Golden Eval Set. Every production incident becomes a permanent regression test so the same hallucination never ships twice. With Ch.03's hybrid retrieval engine and Ch.04's automated verification harness in place, you now own a production-grade RAG stack—ready for Ch.05's transition into stateful AI Agent architectures.
bullets: Match guardrail strictness to risk: soft warnings with citations for low-risk QA; Fail-Closed interception for finance, tax, and healthcare.
Monitor empty-retrieval rate, citation rank, and faithfulness retry rate in production telemetry to spot drift early.
Operate an Eval Flywheel by feeding anonymized production failures back into the Golden Eval Set as permanent regression tests.
sections.callout_title: Architectural Mindset: RAG Is a Measurable Search + Verification Pipeline
sections.callout_body: Turning vague complaints like 'the bot feels worse lately' into 'Golden Set Recall@2 dropped from 0.88 to 0.67 and tax-rate interception jumped 3%' is what separates production AI engineering from fragile demos.

code_walkthrough: recall_at_k(retrieved_ids, relevant_ids, k) guards against empty relevant sets or k <= 0, then intersects set(retrieved_ids[:k]) with relevant_ids to compute Top-K coverage.
mean_reciprocal_rank(runs) iterates over each ranked list, records 1.0 / rank on the very first relevant match and breaks immediately, then averages across all evaluation queries.
check_numeric_faithfulness(answer_text, source_chunks) extracts integers, decimals, and percentages via \b\d+(?:\.\d+)?%? and returns (is_grounded, ungrounded_numbers).

The entrypoint runs three retrieval fixtures plus a US dividend withholding tax check, producing Recall@2: 0.667, MRR: 0.611, True ([]) for the faithful answer, and False (['15%']) for the hallucinated rate.

pitfalls.title: Pitfall 1: Biased Golden Eval Sets Produce High CI Scores and Broken Production UX
pitfalls.symptom: CI reports 0.95 Recall@5 and 100% faithfulness, yet live users complain about typos, edge-case negations, and out-of-scope questions.
pitfalls.root_cause_and_fix: Synthetic 'happy-path' test sets miss messy real-world queries. Regularly sample anonymized low-confidence and empty-retrieval logs into the Golden Set, and include at least 20% negative (unanswerable) fixtures to verify honest abstention.

pitfalls.title: Pitfall 2: Skipping Numeric Normalization Triggers False-Positive Hallucination Blocks
pitfalls.symptom: The source says '1,000 USD' or 'ten percent', and the checker blocks a correct answer containing '1000' or '10%'.
pitfalls.root_cause_and_fix: Raw regex \b\d+(?:\.\d+)?%? does not normalize commas, written words, or equivalent decimals (0.1 vs 10%). Add a lightweight numeric normalization pass before set comparison and escalate flagged edge cases to a lightweight semantic check.

pitfalls.title: Pitfall 3: Running Slow Full-Scale LLM Evals Inside Every Pull Request
pitfalls.symptom: Every PR waits 15-20 minutes for thousands of LLM calls and flakes on rate limits, tempting developers to bypass CI checks.
pitfalls.root_cause_and_fix: Split evals into a Fast PR Gate (<3 minutes, running deterministic Recall@K, MRR with cached models/vectors, and numeric faithfulness unit tests) plus a Nightly Full Eval schedule for expensive LLM-as-a-Judge suites.

quiz.question: In RAG retrieval evaluation, which statement accurately compares Recall@K and MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank)?
options: Recall@K weights rank-1 hits higher than rank-5 hits, whereas MRR ignores rank order completely
Recall@K measures Top-K coverage without distinguishing order inside Top-K; MRR is highly sensitive to the rank position of the first relevant hit (1 / rank)
Recall@K strictly decreases as K grows larger
A high MRR guarantees that multi-document queries never miss a second relevant document
quiz.explanation: Recall@K measures the fraction of relevant documents found anywhere inside Top-K (monotonically non-decreasing with K) without rewarding top rank; MRR averages 1 / rank of the first hit, rewarding top placement but ignoring subsequent relevant documents.

quiz.question: If live metrics show Recall@5 = 0.96 and MRR = 0.90, yet Faithfulness checks fail frequently, what is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Chunking and vector indexing are broken and require replacing the vector database immediately
Retrieval is placing the right evidence at the top; the defect lies in Generation (prompt constraints, conflicting context, or model hallucination) or overly strict faithfulness normalization
Increase K from 5 to 50 to solve the faithfulness failures
quiz.explanation: Decoupling retrieval and generation metrics isolates the fault immediately: high Recall and MRR prove the right evidence reached the top of the prompt, pointing directly to generation constraints, contradictory snippets, or normalization false positives.

quiz.question: What is the best practice for wiring RAG evaluations into GitHub Actions CI/CD without slowing down developers?
options: Run 10,000 full cloud LLM generation evals on every Pull Request regardless of duration
Run fast, deterministic retrieval metrics (Recall@K / MRR with cached artifacts) and numeric faithfulness hard gates on every PR, and schedule full LLM-as-a-Judge suites nightly
Skip CI automation and ask the chatbot two manual questions before each release
Set temperature = 1.0 in CI to test creativity and block merges on random score drops
quiz.explanation: A tiered evaluation pyramid keeps PR checks fast and 100% reproducible while reserving slower, higher-variance semantic judges for Nightly trend monitoring.

interview_faqs.question: How should you choose K in Recall@K, and should every stage of a RAG pipeline track the same K?
interview_faqs.answer: Different pipeline stages require different K values. For first-stage recall (BM25 + ANN), track Recall@20 or Recall@50 to verify relevant chunks reach the reranker pool. After Cross-Encoder reranking and right before prompt assembly, track Recall@3, Recall@5, and MRR to make sure the tight LLM context window contains the highest-value evidence. Single-answer FAQ bots often add a strict Recall@1 (Hit@1) gate.

interview_faqs.question: When MRR is high but Faithfulness is low, in what order should you debug the pipeline?
interview_faqs.answer: Debug in three steps: first inspect 10 failing samples to confirm the faithfulness rule is not misfiring on formatting differences (such as 10% vs 0.1 or 1,000 vs 1000); second check whether retrieved chunks contain outdated or contradictory paragraphs; third tighten system prompt grounding rules (require inline [source_id] citations and explicit abstention when facts are missing) and lower temperature to 0.

interview_faqs.question: How do you avoid false hallucination flags when the model correctly computes a derived figure not written verbatim in the source (such as 100 minus 20 = 80)?
interview_faqs.answer: In high-stakes domains, never rely on an LLM doing mental arithmetic and guessing afterward whether it was right. Have the model invoke a deterministic calculator or Python sandbox tool (Tool Calling) and append the verified tool output to the trusted source corpus. For non-arithmetic logical inference, pair deterministic checks with an LLM-as-a-Judge verifier.

interview_faqs.question: How do you safely evaluate whether upgrading an Embedding model or changing chunk size actually improved your RAG system?
interview_faqs.answer: Replay the exact same version-controlled Golden Eval Set (including common queries, long-tail terms, and negative unanswerable queries) against both candidate pipelines. Compare aggregate Recall@K, MRR, and Faithfulness alongside a per-query regression diff showing every query that flipped from pass to fail. Re-index production only when aggregate metrics improve with zero regressions on critical compliance cases.
